method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023' (2023). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © 2023 European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism. Published by Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved. (read at copyright line of the ESPEN-hosted PDF (free to read at espen.org; DOI 10.1016/j.clnu.2023.07.019, Crossref licence: Elsevier user licence)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. The PDF is two-column, so it was converted with plain `pdftotext` (no `-layout`): `-layout` interleaves the two columns on each line and no sentence could be anchored. Recommendations were taken from the body text, not from the summary table.

claims.claim: **In adults, SBS means less than 200 cm of small bowel left in continuity.** Symptoms of SBS despite a longer remnant are called 'functional SBS'.
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classify SBS by the anatomy that remains:** type 1 is an end small-bowel stoma; type 2 is a jejuno-colic anastomosis; type 3 is a jejuno-ileal anastomosis with the whole colon and ileocaecal valve kept.
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type III (chronic) intestinal failure** is a long-term state in a metabolically stable patient who needs intravenous support for months or years; it may or may not reverse.
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Home parenteral nutrition is the primary, life-saving treatment** for chronic intestinal failure, whether reversible or permanent. (Grade B)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer early to an intestinal failure / rehabilitation centre** with both medical and surgical expertise. This gives the best chance of coming off parenteral nutrition, avoids its failure and allows timely transplant assessment. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Manage SBS through a multidisciplinary team** to get the most from intestinal rehabilitation. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diet should be guided by an expert dietitian**, drawing on the patient's own experience and, ideally, metabolic balance studies, so that the patient can stick to it. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If the colon is still in continuity**, the diet can be rich in complex carbohydrate and low in simple sugars and fat (weakest grade), and should contain plenty of **medium-chain triglyceride (MCT)**, which gives a small gain in energy absorbed over ordinary long-chain fat (Grade B).
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without a colon in continuity**, any ratio of fat to carbohydrate is acceptable, but keep simple sugars low. (weakest grade)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On a low-fat or MCT-substituted diet, watch for essential fatty acid and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.** (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not routinely remove lactose**; restrict it only when intolerance is clinically clear, such as more diarrhoea or stoma output after lactose. (weakest grade)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Glutamine, probiotics and other add-on nutrients are not recommended** to promote intestinal rehabilitation. (weakest grade)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With an end jejunostomy (type 1 SBS)**, patients can salt food freely and should separate drinks from meals. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For borderline dehydration or sodium depletion, an isotonic, high-sodium oral rehydration solution** can replace sodium lost from the stoma. (weakest grade)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A secretory, high-output jejunostomy needs low-sodium drinks cut back**: both hypotonic fluids (water, tea, coffee, alcohol) and hypertonic ones (fruit juice, cola) increase stoma output. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An H2-receptor antagonist or PPI may reduce faecal fluid and sodium losses**, especially in the first six months after surgery and when output is over 2 L/d (weakest grade); it can also be continued long term in individual patients (GPP).
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral loperamide is the antidiarrhoeal of choice** to cut stoma fluid and sodium losses (Grade A), preferred over codeine or opium because it is neither addictive nor sedating (Grade A).
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Octreotide can be tried for a high-output jejunostomy**, mainly soon after resection, when fluid and electrolytes stay hard to control despite standard measures. Monitor for fluid retention and possible harm to intestinal adaptation. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antibiotics are not routine when the colon is preserved**, because colonic fermentation salvages energy; occasional courses can help suspected bacterial overgrowth with dysmotility or blind loops. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral absorption of any drug is uncertain in SBS.** Prescribe individually, titrate to effect or levels, and consider parenteral, transdermal or rectal routes when absorption is limited. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider an intestinal growth factor when a patient still needs parenteral nutrition after adaptation**, usually twelve to 24 months after the last resection, if there is no contraindication. (Grade B)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Teduglutide is the first-choice growth factor** for carefully selected candidates. (Grade A)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Before starting, exclude polyps and cancer:** colonoscopy (if any colon or rectum remains), gastroscopy and abdominal ultrasound for everyone, which also clarify strictures, blind loops or active Crohn's disease. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only experienced SBS clinicians should prescribe it**, with the means to measure benefit objectively (fluid, electrolyte and energy balance by standard protocol) against adverse effects, risk and cost. Explain the chance of weaning, the duration, what happens on stopping and the monitoring required. (GPP)
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At resection, keep as much bowel as possible** to avoid parenteral nutrition dependence, and **restore intestinal continuity whenever possible** (both Grade B). Bowel-lengthening procedures may suit selected patients (weakest grade).
claims.locator: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), Clinical Nutrition 42 (2023) 1940–2021, 'ESPEN guideline on chronic intestinal failure in adults – Update 2023', 2023, https://www.espen.org/files/ESPEN-Guidelines/ESPEN_guideline_on_chronic_intestinal_failure_in_adults.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
